rule: Typed receivers (decision A, all statically typed languages and typed PHP/Groovy declarations): a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including `$var->prop` / `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). | Constructor / initializer call: `Type#<init>`. | Code outside a method body: the caller is its location. Field/val initializer → `Type#field`; C# property accessor → `Type#Prop` (get) / `Type#Prop=` (set); Ruby setter → `Type#x=`; `static {}` block → `Type#<clinit>`. Non-lazy initializers also get an `implicit` edge from `<clinit>`/`<init>`; lazy ones do not.
source: KNOWN_GAP: ?. calls and target-typed new() are missed
notes: Target-typed `new()` constructs the declared type of its target: the field seen (List<string> → System.Collections.Generic.List#<init>, medium, type resolved through the file's single using-directive; generic argument dropped), the field logger (App.Logger#<init>, high) and the local backup. The field initializer's caller is App.Service#seen plus the implicit <init> edge (high: callee defined in the scan). `x?.M()` is a call of M on x (null-conditional only skips it when x is null): logger/backup are typed by their declarations (Logger#Log, high), seen by its field type (List#Add, medium).
